Strong pathogenicity (z=0.93); mild natural tolerance (Y ~4.3% among homologs) slightly tempers confidence but phenotype signal keeps it near the top.

history.rationale: Arg in the RGDP catalytic loop is often functionally critical; loss of positive charge should impair substrate/FAD interactions.
Lowest pathogenicity of the pool (0.629) and a conservative charge-loss substitution; demoted but retained as backup.
Lowest phenotype z (0.63) among the pool despite conservation support; remains the weakest LOF candidate and stays as backup.
Buried/flexible glycine in the catalytic core; substitution with bulky charged Arg likely introduces steric/backbone strain abolishing activity.
Strong pathogenicity (0.826); Gly->Arg introduces bulk/charge at a likely conserved glycine, plausibly destabilizing the fold.
Solid pathogenicity (z=0.83), zero mutant frequency, and low ESM plausibility; charge introduction (Gly→Arg) at conserved position is plausibly destabilizing/LOF.
Conserved proline (PIVPGIFP region) likely fixes local geometry; Gly substitution increases flexibility and may disrupt active-site loop.
Highest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy score (0.97) and Pro->Gly removes a likely rigid backbone constraint; strongest disruption candidate.

Highest AlphaMissense pathogenicity (z=0.97), zero mutant frequency in MSA, and near-zero ESM plausibility all coherently indicate a strongly disruptive substitution at a conserved Pro. Confidence slightly raised.
Histidine in the HMTCC motif may participate in catalysis/metal coordination; bulky aromatic replacement could abolish activity.
Very high pathogenicity (0.927); H127 lies in the catalytic domain region and His-to-Tyr can disrupt cofactor/active-site chemistry.
Strong pathogenicity (z=0.93) but Y appears at 4.3% frequency among homologs, indicating some natural tolerance which mildly weakens LOF confidence. Kept near top given phenotype dominance.
